description: The three Sloth chaos circuits on one panel, apathy, inertia and torpor, with a CV input for two of them and a pair of combined outputs

params.text: Adds up to 10 kilohms to a fixed 100 kilohms in that circuit, which changes how long it spends around one of its two attractors rather than the other; it does not change the rate

inputs.text: Added into that circuit after being clamped to -12V to 12V; it nudges the chaotic path and also offsets that circuit's Z output

outputs.text: The narrower-swinging of that circuit's two chaotic voltages
The wider-swinging of that circuit's two chaotic voltages, the one the lamp above the column follows: green while it is positive, red while it is negative, full brightness at 2V
That circuit's Y voltage inverted, with a fifth of its CV input added
The inertia circuit's Y voltage inverted; inertia has no CV input, so nothing is added to it
The three Z voltages combined while that total is negative, down to the circuit's own limit, and 0V at any other time; the total is 0.7 times torpor's Z less apathy's Z and inertia's Z added together
The three Z voltages combined while that total is positive, and 0V at any other time; the total is 0.7 times torpor's Z less apathy's Z and inertia's Z added together

notes: there is nothing to patch in to make this work: all three circuits run from the moment the module is added and every output is moving straight away.
inertia has neither a knob nor a CV input; one turn around its attractors takes roughly 30 to 40 minutes, against 60 to 90 seconds for apathy and 15 to 30 seconds for torpor.
the Z outputs here are the inverted form of the Y output the single Sloth modules give, which is why the panel has three outputs per circuit where they have two.
